title: Evaluation of two expressions
statement: Let $Z$ be admissible compiler size data of word size $W$, with state $\sigma$ represented in a stack frame at depth $q$ by memory $m$, where $1\le q$ and $q+F\le Q$. Suppose the code at $\mathrm{pos}$ begins with the compiled code for expressions $a$ and $b$ using temporary slots $0$ and $1$, respectively; both expressions have width at most $F$ and are safe under the limits and state $\sigma$. Then some memory $m'$ is reached after $a$'s size plus $b$'s size machine steps, at program counter $\mathrm{pos}+a.\mathrm{size}+b.\mathrm{size}$, with temporary slots $0$ and $1$ containing the words encoding the respective values of $a$ and $b$ in $\sigma$. The memories agree outside the scratch-address set for $F$.
